claims.text: A binomial name is used in the same form in every language, so it identifies an organism without the confusion of common names, which differ between languages and regions and can be shared by different organisms. Closely related species share a genus: the lion Panthera leo and the leopard Panthera pardus share the genus Panthera.

claims.text: To construct a key, first choose features that can be seen clearly and that differ between the organisms, then write a couplet whose two statements split the set into two smaller sets. Repeat with each smaller set until every organism has its own name, and finally test the key by identifying each organism with it.

claims.text: A key for local organisms should use features that can be seen in the field, such as the presence of horns, the number of leaflets or the type of body covering. Features that vary with age or season, such as size or flower colour, make poor choices, and a key identifies correctly just the organisms it was built for.

claims.text: In the biological species concept a species is a group of organisms that can interbreed in natural conditions to produce fertile offspring, and that do not breed in this way with organisms of other such groups. An organism is a single individual; a species is the group into which it is placed.

claims.text: In the morphological species concept a species is a group of organisms that share observable structural features and differ in them from other such groups. It can be applied to preserved specimens and fossils, but its weakness is that members of one species may differ in appearance, for example males and females or young and adults, while different species may look alike.

claims.text: In the ecological species concept a species is defined by its niche, the role of the organism: the conditions it tolerates, the resources it uses and its interactions with other organisms. In the behavioural species concept a species is defined by shared behaviour, such as a courtship call or display, which leads members to mate with their own species.

claims.text: The biological species concept depends on observing or testing interbreeding, so it cannot be applied to fossils, to preserved specimens or to organisms that reproduce asexually. A horse and a donkey can mate, but the offspring, a mule, is usually sterile, so by this concept they are separate species.
